structured.answer: I'd pick A, the single tall column. Each piece has its name in Hebrew right beside it, and below it in big letters is what's left in your hand: 66,513 ₪ in the keren against 19,595 ₪ in the other account. It shows plainly that the employer's yellow part, 54,000 ₪, is what makes joining worth it.

stuck.where: Option A, the striped pink piece on top of the keren column with "מס במשיכה −13,974 ₪"
stuck.why: It sits on top of the column, so I wasn't sure whether the 66,513 already has the tax taken off or not. The minus sign made me stop.

stuck.where: Option B, the pink striped box with −13,974 floating at the top
stuck.why: Boxes going up and down, each starting where the last one ended. I couldn't follow them from right to left, and the red minus box was the first thing I looked at.

stuck.where: The row of 12 small bars at the top of each option, with the circle on 5 or 6
stuck.why: I didn't understand that I was supposed to choose a year. The note says you can drag it, but I don't touch things like that.

findings.what: The page is black with grey and pale writing. The small print under the charts and in the example I couldn't read even with my glasses.
findings.where: The whole page, especially the example paragraph and the lines under the columns

findings.what: The red minus numbers (−13,974, −594, −866) catch the eye first and scare you off, even though the bottom line is positive.
In B, the boxes float in the air and the labels underneath are tiny. I couldn't follow what adds up to what.
The example opens with English letters and fund names. That gives the feeling it's a gamble and not for me.
findings.where: The orange/grey example paragraph above option A

findings.what: The yellow and the dark green look alike to me on the black background.
It isn't clear whether the tax on top of the column comes off the total or not.
findings.where: Option A, the top of the keren column

findings.what: Nowhere does it say whether the money can go down.
